learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude for applying knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

syllabus_topics: Real numbers. Inequalities. Absolute value. Intervals
Elementary functions of one and several variables. Function composition and inverse functions
General convergence criterion. Absolute convergence. Conditional convergence. Leibniz's criterion
Differentiation of functions. Definitions. Interpretation (local and absolute maxima and minima, concavity and convexity, asymptotes, inflection points). Rules
Taylor polynomial. Taylor series. Evaluation of limits using the Taylor polynomial
Riemann integral of a single variable. Evaluation of definite integrals
Geometrical applications: lengths, areas and volumes. Calculation of volumes by cross-sections
teaching_methods: Guided activities (e.g., written reports, oral or audiovisual presentations, problem-solving, practical case studies, use of computer-based calculation or simulation tools)
assessment_rules: The final grading system is expressed numerically: 0-4.9 Fail, 5.0-6.9 Pass, 7.0-8.9 Good, 9.0-10 Very Good. A minimum mark of 5.0 must be obtained in the final on-campus examination, and a minimum of 4.0 in the application exercises (SE11), for the assessment components to be combined. The resulting weighted average mark must be at least 5.0 to pass the module. Missing more than 25% of face-to-face classes without valid reason may result in being barred from the ordinary examination.
